chunks: 3254 - And ʿAmr ibn Thābit narrated from his father, from Saʿd ibn Ṭarīf, from al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubātah, who said:

A woman was brought to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. An old man had married her, and when he had intercourse with her, he died upon her stomach. Then she gave birth to a child, so his sons claimed that she had committed fornication and testified against her. ʿUmar ordered that she be stoned. Then they passed by ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام, and she said: “O cousin of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, I am wronged, and this is my proof.” So he said: “Bring your proof.” Then she handed him a document, and he read it. Then he said: “This woman informs you of the day he married her, the day he had intercourse with her, and how his intercourse with her was. Return the woman.”

Then when the next day came, ʿAlī عليه السلام called for children of the same age who were playing, and among them was her son. He said to them: “Play.” So they played until, when the play had distracted them, he shouted at them, and they stood up. The boy who was the woman’s son stood up leaning on his palms. Then ʿAlī عليه السلام called him forward, gave him inheritance from his father, and flogged his brothers who had made the false accusation, each one with the prescribed punishment.
Then ʿUmar said to him: “How did you do this?” He said: “I recognized the old man’s weakness from the boy’s leaning upon his palms.”

key_terms.الْمُفْتَرِينَ: those who falsely accused or fabricated a charge
key_terms.تُرْجَمَ: to be stoned as a legal punishment
key_terms.حُجَّتِي: my proof or evidence in support of my claim
key_terms.ضَعْفَ الشَّيْخِ: the frailty or weakness of the old man
key_terms.فَوَرَّثَهُ: he made him inherit from his father

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام prove a child’s lineage and prevent a wrongful punishment in a case of false accusation?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts a judicial case in which Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام overturned a wrongful accusation of adultery through careful examination and reasoning. He established the child’s paternity, restored the child’s inheritance rights, and punished the false accusers, showing the role of just judgment and discernment in legal rulings.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3254 - Amr ibn Thabit narrated from his father, from Sad ibn Tarif, from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said:

A woman was brought before Umar ibn al-Khattab. She had married an old man who died while lying on top of her after consummating the marriage. Later, she gave birth to a child.
The old man's sons accused her of adultery and testified against her.
Umar ordered that she be stoned.
As they were leading her away, they passed by Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as).
She called out: "O cousin of the Messenger of Allah (swt)! I am wronged, and this is my evidence."
Imam (as) said: "Present your evidence."
She handed him a letter, and Imam (as) read it.
Then Imam (as) said: "This woman is informing you of the date of her marriage, the date of consummation, and how it occurred. Return the woman."

The next day, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) summoned some children who were of the same age as the woman's child and told them to play.
They played until they became distracted.
Then Imam (as) called out to them suddenly, and they all stood up, including the woman's child, who stood leaning on both his palms for support.
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) called the child forward, confirmed his paternity, and ruled that he inherit from his father.
He then ordered the brothers, who had falsely accused the woman, to be lashed one by one as the punishment for false accusation.

Umar asked Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as): "How did you reach this judgment?"
Imam (as) replied: "I recognized the frailty of the old man from the way the child leaned on his palms to stand up."
